events.handwritten: Tables up to 8, last one at 7pm

line.text: Let's start with a time this went wrong. Can you think of a recent chat reply that promised a table booking and caused trouble, like a group turning up with no table or a booking that shouldn't have been accepted?

Oh God, yes, the big one was a Saturday booking. The chat took a table for fourteen at half seven in the evening, and we were closing and didn't have the room, so I had to ring them myself to cancel. I was mortified, honestly, the poor people were already planning their night.

events.text: ShiftGuard thinks about what to ask next

line.text: That sounds stressful, and I'm sorry they had to be let down like that. What is the largest group the chat should ever be allowed to book for on its own, and is that number itself okay, or should the chat hand bigger groups to you?
Eight is the most the chat can book on its own, and eight is fine. Anything bigger, the chat should pass it to me, because I'd rather ring them myself and sort out the room.

events.text: ShiftGuard thinks about what to ask next

line.text: Got it, eight is the most the chat can book alone, and eight itself is fine. The Saturday booking was also near closing, so does the limit hold at every time of day and every day of the week, or are there times when the chat shouldn't take a booking even for a small group?

Ah, the time matters too, love. The chat can only book while we're open, and the last booking has to be at seven in the evening, since we close at eight. Seven exactly is grand, but nothing after that. And nothing before seven in the morning either. Anything outside those times, it should pass to me.

events.text: ShiftGuard thinks about what to ask next

line.text: Thanks, that's clear. Does this hold every day of the week, including weekends and holidays, or are there any days or situations where the chat should pass a booking to you even if it fits these times and sizes?

Every day, love, we're open seven days, so the same times hold, weekends included. I haven't really thought about public holidays for the chat, to be honest. If it's unsure about a holiday, it should just pass it to me and I'll sort it out.

events.text: ShiftGuard thinks about what to ask next

line.text: Let me check I have it right. The chat can book a table only for groups of up to eight people, and only for a time from 7:00 am up to and including 7:00 pm, every day of the week. Anything larger, or at any other time, goes to you. If it's unsure about a public holiday, it passes the booking to you. Is that right?

Yes, that's it exactly, love. Up to eight people, between seven in the morning and seven at night, every day. Anything bigger or outside those times, the chat passes it to me, and if it's a holiday and it's not sure, same thing. Sorted.

events.text: ShiftGuard thinks about what to ask next

line.text: Thanks, that's all clear. I've got the rule down as: the chat can book a table only for groups of up to eight, between 7:00 am and 7:00 pm inclusive, every day, and passes anything else to you, including unsure public holidays.

rule.title: Chat books tables only for up to eight, 7am to 7pm
rule.ownerWords: The chat can only book for groups of eight or fewer, and only during opening hours up to the last booking at seven in the evening. Anything bigger, or at any other time, it should pass to the owner. If it's unsure about a public holiday, it passes it on too.
rule.precise: Applies to every day of the week, weekends included. The chat may book only if the party size is 8 or fewer AND the requested time is no earlier than 7:00 am and no later than 7:00 pm (7:00 pm exactly is allowed). Anything with more than 8 people, or a time before 7:00 am or after 7:00 pm, must be passed to the owner. If the chat is unsure whether a public holiday applies, it must pass the booking to the owner.
rule.exceptions: None. Public holidays: if unsure, pass to the owner.
rule.whyKind: Party size and booking time can be checked directly against the stated numbers, so code can decide them from the facts alone; the unsure-holiday case is handled by passing it to the owner.
